## United Arab Emirates
[edit]
The UAE relies has over 70 desalination plants, and relies on desalination for 42% of its drinking water.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-131) The hosts some of the world's largest desalination plants, which are listed in the table above.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-132) The include the Jebel Ali desalination plant in Dubai, a dual-purpose facility, uses multistage flash distillation and is the largest in the world, capable of producing 2,227,600 m 3 (2,913,600 cu yd) of water per day. Al Taweelah RO is the world's largest reverse osmosis desalination plant, producing 909,200 m 3 (1,189,200 cu yd) of water per day.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-133)
Some of the smaller ones include:

## United Arab Emirates
*   Kalba 15,000 m 3/day built for Sharjah Electricity and Water Authority completed 2010 (operator CH2MHill)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-134)  
*   Khor Fakkan 22,500 m 3/day (operator CH2MHill)  
*   Ghalilah RAK 68,000 m 3/day (operator Aquatech)  
*   Hamriyah 90,000 m 3/day (operator Aqua Engineering)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-Aquatech-107)  
*   Al Zawrah 27,000 m 3/day (operator Aqua Engineering)  
*   Layyah I 22,500 m 3/day (operator CH2MHill)  
*   Emayil & Saydiat Island ≈20,000 m 3/day (operator Aqua EPC)  
*   Al Yasat Al Soghrih Island 2M gallons per day (GPD) or 9,000 m 3/day  
*   A seawater greenhouse was constructed on Al Aryam Island, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates in 2000.

## United Kingdom and Crown dependencies
[edit]
The first large-scale plant in the United Kingdom, the Thames Water Desalination Plant, was built in Beckton, east London for Thames Water by Acciona Agua.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-135) It was built in 2010 at a cost of £250m. The plant provides up to 150 million litres of drinking water each day (150,000 cubic metres) – enough for nearly one million people.
The desalination plant located near La Rosière, La Corbière, Jersey, is operated by Jersey Water. Built in 1970 in an abandoned quarry, it was the first in the British Isles.
The original plant used a multistage flash (MSF) distillation process, whereby seawater was boiled under vacuum, evaporated and condensed into a freshwater distillate. In 1997, the MSF plant reached the end of its operational life and was replaced with a modern reverse osmosis plant.
Its maximum power demand is 1,750 kW, and the output capacity is 6,000 cubic meters per day. Specific energy consumption is 6.8 kWh/m 3.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-136)
There are a dozen different desalination projects in the state of Texas, both for desalinating groundwater and desalinating seawater from the Gulf of Mexico. Corpus Christi is currently in the process of finding a contractor to start the development of one in the Corpus Christi ship channel.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-137) However, currently there are no seawater desalination plants earmarked for municipal purposes.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-138)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-139)

## United Kingdom and Crown dependencies
*   El Paso: Brackish groundwater has been treated at the El Paso, Texas, plant since around 2004. It produces 27,500,000 US gallons (104,000,000 L; 22,900,000 imp gal) of fresh water daily (about 25% of total freshwater deliveries) by reverse osmosis.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-140) The plant's water cost–largely representing the cost of energy–is about 2.1 times higher than ordinary groundwater production.
California has 17 desalination plants in the works, either partially constructed or through exploration and planning phases.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-pricey-141) The list of locations includes Bay Point, in the Delta, Redwood City, seven in the Santa Cruz / Monterey Bay, Cambria, Oceaneo, Redondo Beach, Huntington Beach, Dana Point, Camp Pendleton, Oceanside and Carlsbad.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-142)

## United Kingdom and Crown dependencies
*   Carlsbad: The [Claude "Bud" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_%22Bud%22_Lewis_Carlsbad_Desalination_Plant "Claude \"Bud\" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant") was constructed at a cost of $1 billion by Poseidon Resources and was the largest desalination plant in the United States when it went online December 14, 2015.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-143) It produces 50 million gallons a day to 110,000 customers throughout San Diego County.  
*   Monterey County: Sand City, two miles north of Monterey, with a population of 334, is the only city in California completely supplied with water from a desalination plant.  
*   Santa Barbara: The Charles Meyer Desalination Facility was constructed in Santa Barbara, California, in 1991–92 as a temporary emergency water supply in response to severe drought.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-145) While it has a high operating cost, the facility only needs to operate infrequently, allowing Santa Barbara to use its other supplies more extensively.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-146)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-147) The plant was re-activated in the spring of 2017.
RO production train, North Cape Coral RO Plant
In 1977, Cape Coral, Florida became the first municipality in the United States to use the RO process on a large scale with an initial operating capacity of 3 million gallons per day. By 1985, due to the rapid growth in population of Cape Coral, the city had the largest low pressure reverse osmosis plant in the world, capable of producing 15 MGD.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-148)

The global desalination market is witnessing strong growth as countries increasingly invest in alternative water sources to address rising water scarcity, rapid urbanization, industrial expansion, and climate-related stress on freshwater supplies. As per Blackridge Research’s Global Desalination Market Outlook, the market is projected to reach USD 38–59 billion by 2032–2034, growing at a CAGR of 8.5–10%. Reverse osmosis technology continues to dominate the sector due to its improving energy efficiency and lower operating costs.
The Middle East remains the global center of desalination development, led by Saudi Arabia, which operates some of the world’s largest desalination facilities. Major desalination projects such as the Ras Al Khair Desalination Plant, Jebel Ali Desalination Plant, Fujairah Desalination Plant, Taweelah Desalination Plant, and Jubail Water and Power Company (JWAP) highlight the scale of investment in securing long-term water supply across the region.
This article outlines the top 10 desalination plants in the world based on their capacities.

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Ras AL Khair Desalination Plant
The Ras AL Khair Desalination Plant is one of the largest desalination plants in the world. It was commissioned in April 2014 and produces 228 MIGD (Million Imperial Gallons per day) or 2,998,000 cubic meters/day. This large desalination plant is built and owned by SWCC (Saline Water Conversion Corporation of Saudi Arabia) at a project cost of USD 7.2 Billion and is mentioned in Guinness world record.
It is located on the eastern coast of Ras AL Khair Industrial City and performs both MSF (Multi-flash filtration) and RO (Reverse Osmosis). It supplies clean drinking water to Riyadh and Hafr AL-Batin, the largest cities in Saudi Arabia, thus one of the largest desalination plants in Saudi Arabia. Additionally, it includes a power generation plant with a capacity of 2400 MW.

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Jebel Ali Desalination Plant
The Jebel Ali Power and Desalination Plant is one the largest single-site desalination facility in the world. It is also known as one of the largest desalination plants in the UAE and Middle East with a capacity of 490 MIGD (2,228,000 cubic meters per day). Located in the Southwest Palm Islands, it is one of the most renowned desalination plants in Dubai built at an estimated project cost of USD 3 Billion.
It uses Reverse osmosis technology and is considered one of the biggest desalination plant in the world. Mostly multi-stage flash (43 MSF units, 427 MIGD) plus 2 SWRO plants (63 MIGD); Guinness single-site record (Oct 2022). The Jebel Ali Power and Desalination Plant has a power plant with a capacity to produce 9,547 MW. The Complex has two plants 1 and 2 for power generation and water desalination. Plant -1 with a production capacity of 2,761 MW cconsists of stations D, E, and G. Plant-2 with a production capacity of 6,786 MW consists of stations K, L, and M. The desalination plant was built by Acciona and BESIX Group and is currently operated by DEWA (Dubai Electricity and Water Authority).

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Fujairah Desalination Plant
The Fujairah desalination plant is one of the largest desalination plants in Abu Dhabi. It is a hybrid desalination plant that provides water security through large scale desalination and electricity. The Fujairah F1 Desalination plant was built at an estimated project cost of USD 650-700 Million and the Fujairah F2 Desalination plant was built at a project cost of USD 2.17 Billion. The total capacity of the desalination plant is 230 MIGD.
The 1,045,361 cubic meters of Abu Dhabi water per day is reducing water shortage through consistent water supply in Abu Dhabi.
On 18th February 2025, ​Etihad Water & Electricity UAE issued tenders for the development of an Independent Water Project (IWP) in Fujairah, one of the northern emirates. The bid submission deadlines are set for February 17 and 18, 2025. Complete details of the project are not yet disclosed.

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Shuaiba 3 Desalination Plant
The Shuaiba 3 Desalination Plant is one of the biggest desalination plants in the world with a capacity of 600,000 cubic meters per day. This project is currently under construction and is built at a cost of USD 821 Million. The plant is likely to be commissioned in May 2025.
It is built by ACWA and WHEC(Water and Electricity Holding Company) PIF. The Shuaiba 3 will be using SWRO (Sea water Reverse Osmosis) desalination technology to provide potable drinking water. The power for the desalination plant is met through Grid-SEC and [Captive Solar PV](https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/solar-thermal-vs-solar-photovoltaic-pv-panel-difference-efficiency-explained#:~:text=Solar%20thermal%20collects%20sunlight%20to,PV%20is%20used%20during%20summers.).
​The Shuaiba 3 Desalination Plant in Saudi Arabia is set for commercial operation in May 2025. It was built by Doosan Enerbility, with an investment of SAR 3.07 billion (USD 821 million). It will be producing 600,000 cubic meters of water per day. ​

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Carlsbad Desalination Plant
The Carlsbad Desalination plant in San Diego County, California is one of the biggest desalination plants in the western hemisphere. It is built at a project cost of USD 922 Million, by Poseidon Resources Corporation. The desalination plant produces 50 MIGD equals to 1,89,000 cubic meters per day.
The desalinated seawater from the Carlsbad plant fulfills 10% of the total drinking water supply of San Diego and 2,440 cubic feet of water a year sufficient for 300,000 people. The water from Carlsbad Desalination plant is purchased by Carlsbad agencies and is supplied to San Diego County Water Authority (SDCWA).

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Minjur Desalination Plant
The Minjur Desalination Plant is one of the first largest desalination plants in India with a capacity of 100 MLD (100,000 cubic meters per day). It is built in Tamil Nadu, a state in India by CWDL (Chennai Water Desalination) for CMWSSB (Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board) under DBOOT Contract (Design, Build, Own, Operate, Transfer).
The seawater desalination plant was commissioned in 2010 and was built at a project cost of INR 5.15 Billion (USD 62 Million). Using RO desalination technology, the Minjur Desalination plant provides potable water to 500,000 people in Chennai. It is one of the largest water resources for the people of Chennai.

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## Desalination Plants and its Future
According to the Economic World Forum, by 2030, there could be a global shortfall of fresh water source by 40% with an increase in overall population from 8 billion in 2024 to 9.7 billion by 2050. Likewise, Sub-Saharan Africa is expected to see a 163% increase in water demand over the coming years.
Desalination technologies like reverse osmosis, thermal desalination and multi-flash, are serving as a useful tool in the seawater desalination process. However, with the increased demand and supply predicted new desalination technology - Wave powered desalination is innovated. In this, specialized devices float over the ocean water surface capturing the waves to produce electricity which is used to power RO Desalination technology. The Wave powered desalination is highly advantageous for floating-based desalination plants that can improve energy efficiency by reducing the emissions occurring through traditional use of fossil fuels.
The use of Solar power to run the RO plants is a boost available at a reduced cost of 20% compared to traditional desalination methods and can be implied in countries abundant with sunlight. Additionally, this helps reduce the use of harmful chemicals used during the desalination process. Thus, the desalination sector continues to evolve with growing advancements in the field.

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## Conclusion
Desalination plants with innovations continue to serve as a reliable source of drinking water for billions across the globe. Desalination plants like Ras al Khair, Shuaiba 3, Jebel ali desalination plant, Tampa bay seawater desalination plant are providing potable water for millions of people everyday. Several countries are investing into the development of the desalination industry, thus desalination plants promise to be a major water lifeline for the future. The global desalination market is witnessing strong growth as countries increasingly invest in alternative water sources to address rising water scarcity, rapid urbanization, industrial expansion, and climate-related stress on freshwater supplies. As per Blackridge Research’s Global Desalination Market Outlook, the market is projected to reach USD 38–59 billion by 2032–2034, growing at a CAGR of 8.5–10%. Reverse osmosis technology continues to dominate the sector due to its improving energy efficiency and lower operating costs.
The Middle East remains the global center of desalination development, led by Saudi Arabia, which operates some of the world’s largest desalination facilities. Major desalination projects such as the Ras Al Khair Desalination Plant, Jebel Ali Desalination Plant, Fujairah Desalination Plant, Taweelah Desalination Plant, and Jubail Water and Power Company (JWAP) highlight the scale of investment in securing long-term water supply across the region.
This article outlines the top 10 desalination plants in the world based on their capacities.

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Ras AL Khair Desalination Plant
The Ras AL Khair Desalination Plant is one of the largest desalination plants in the world. It was commissioned in April 2014 and produces 228 MIGD (Million Imperial Gallons per day) or 2,998,000 cubic meters/day. This large desalination plant is built and owned by SWCC (Saline Water Conversion Corporation of Saudi Arabia) at a project cost of USD 7.2 Billion and is mentioned in Guinness world record.
It is located on the eastern coast of Ras AL Khair Industrial City and performs both MSF (Multi-flash filtration) and RO (Reverse Osmosis). It supplies clean drinking water to Riyadh and Hafr AL-Batin, the largest cities in Saudi Arabia, thus one of the largest desalination plants in Saudi Arabia. Additionally, it includes a power generation plant with a capacity of 2400 MW.

# 10 Largest Desalination Plants in the World (2026)
## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Jebel Ali Desalination Plant
The Jebel Ali Power and Desalination Plant is one the largest single-site desalination facility in the world. It is also known as one of the largest desalination plants in the UAE and Middle East with a capacity of 490 MIGD (2,228,000 cubic meters per day). Located in the Southwest Palm Islands, it is one of the most renowned desalination plants in Dubai built at an estimated project cost of USD 3 Billion.
It uses Reverse osmosis technology and is considered one of the biggest desalination plant in the world. Mostly multi-stage flash (43 MSF units, 427 MIGD) plus 2 SWRO plants (63 MIGD); Guinness single-site record (Oct 2022). The Jebel Ali Power and Desalination Plant has a power plant with a capacity to produce 9,547 MW. The Complex has two plants 1 and 2 for power generation and water desalination. Plant -1 with a production capacity of 2,761 MW cconsists of stations D, E, and G. Plant-2 with a production capacity of 6,786 MW consists of stations K, L, and M. The desalination plant was built by Acciona and BESIX Group and is currently operated by DEWA (Dubai Electricity and Water Authority).

The Fujairah desalination plant is one of the largest desalination plants in Abu Dhabi. The 1,045,361 cubic meters of Abu Dhabi water per day is reducing water shortage through consistent water supply in Abu Dhabi.

## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Shuaiba 3 Desalination Plant
The Shuaiba 3 Desalination Plant is one of the biggest desalination plants in the world with a capacity of 600,000 cubic meters per day. This project is currently under construction and is built at a cost of USD 821 Million. The plant is likely to be commissioned in May 2025.
It is built by ACWA and WHEC(Water and Electricity Holding Company) PIF. The Shuaiba 3 will be using SWRO (Sea water Reverse Osmosis) desalination technology to provide potable drinking water. The power for the desalination plant is met through Grid-SEC and [Captive Solar PV](https://www.blackridgeresearch.com/blog/solar-thermal-vs-solar-photovoltaic-pv-panel-difference-efficiency-explained#:~:text=Solar%20thermal%20collects%20sunlight%20to,PV%20is%20used%20during%20summers.).
​The Shuaiba 3 Desalination Plant in Saudi Arabia is set for commercial operation in May 2025. It was built by Doosan Enerbility, with an investment of SAR 3.07 billion (USD 821 million). It will be producing 600,000 cubic meters of water per day. ​

## List of Largest Desalination Plants in the World _(Based on Capacity)_
### Carlsbad Desalination Plant
The Carlsbad Desalination plant in San Diego County, California is one of the biggest desalination plants in the western hemisphere. It is built at a project cost of USD 922 Million, by Poseidon Resources Corporation. The desalination plant produces 50 MIGD equals to 1,89,000 cubic meters per day.
The desalinated seawater from the Carlsbad plant fulfills 10% of the total drinking water supply of San Diego and 2,440 cubic feet of water a year sufficient for 300,000 people. The water from Carlsbad Desalination plant is purchased by Carlsbad agencies and is supplied to San Diego County Water Authority (SDCWA).

### Minjur Desalination Plant
The Minjur Desalination Plant is one of the first largest desalination plants in India with a capacity of 100 MLD (100,000 cubic meters per day). The seawater desalination plant was commissioned in 2010 and was built at a project cost of INR 5.15 Billion (USD 62 Million). Using RO desalination technology, the Minjur Desalination plant provides potable water to 500,000 people in Chennai. It is one of the largest water resources for the people of Chennai.

## Desalination Plants and its Future
According to the Economic World Forum, by 2030, there could be a global shortfall of fresh water source by 40% with an increase in overall population from 8 billion in 2024 to 9.7 billion by 2050. Likewise, Sub-Saharan Africa is expected to see a 163% increase in water demand over the coming years.
Desalination technologies like reverse osmosis, thermal desalination and multi-flash, are serving as a useful tool in the seawater desalination process. However, with the increased demand and supply predicted new desalination technology - Wave powered desalination is innovated. In this, specialized devices float over the ocean water surface capturing the waves to produce electricity which is used to power RO Desalination technology. The Wave powered desalination is highly advantageous for floating-based desalination plants that can improve energy efficiency by reducing the emissions occurring through traditional use of fossil fuels.
The use of Solar power to run the RO plants is a boost available at a reduced cost of 20% compared to traditional desalination methods and can be implied in countries abundant with sunlight. Additionally, this helps reduce the use of harmful chemicals used during the desalination process. Thus, the desalination sector continues to evolve with growing advancements in the field.

## United Kingdom and Crown dependencies
[edit]
The first large-scale plant in the United Kingdom, the Thames Water Desalination Plant, was built in Beckton, east London for Thames Water by Acciona Agua.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-135) It was built in 2010 at a cost of £250m. The plant provides up to 150 million litres of drinking water each day (150,000 cubic metres) – enough for nearly one million people.
The desalination plant located near La Rosière, La Corbière, Jersey, is operated by Jersey Water. Built in 1970 in an abandoned quarry, it was the first in the British Isles.
The original plant used a multistage flash (MSF) distillation process, whereby seawater was boiled under vacuum, evaporated and condensed into a freshwater distillate. In 1997, the MSF plant reached the end of its operational life and was replaced with a modern reverse osmosis plant.
Its maximum power demand is 1,750 kW, and the output capacity is 6,000 cubic meters per day. Specific energy consumption is 6.8 kWh/m 3.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-136)
There are a dozen different desalination projects in the state of Texas, both for desalinating groundwater and desalinating seawater from the Gulf of Mexico. Corpus Christi is currently in the process of finding a contractor to start the development of one in the Corpus Christi ship channel.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-137) However, currently there are no seawater desalination plants earmarked for municipal purposes.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-138)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-139)

## United Kingdom and Crown dependencies
*   Carlsbad: The [Claude "Bud" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_%22Bud%22_Lewis_Carlsbad_Desalination_Plant "Claude \"Bud\" Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant") was constructed at a cost of $1 billion by Poseidon Resources and was the largest desalination plant in the United States when it went online December 14, 2015.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desalination_by_country#cite_note-143) It produces 50 million gallons a day to 110,000 customers throughout San Diego County.
